purpose: Amivantamab-vmjw is used to treat a certain type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has specific gene changes called EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations. It is typically used when the cancer has gotten worse during or after chemotherapy. It may also be used in combination with other medicines depending on your specific situation.
how_it_works: This medicine is a special protein called a bispecific antibody, which means it can attach to two different targets at the same time — one called EGFR and another called MET — both of which help cancer cells grow. By blocking both of these targets, it helps stop the cancer cells from growing and spreading. It also helps your own immune system recognize and attack the cancer cells.
common_side_effects: Rash or skin problems (including dry or itchy skin), low levels of albumin (a blood protein), swelling in the legs or arms, shortness of breath, nausea, fatigue, constipation, changes in certain lab values like low magnesium or potassium, and infusion-related reactions during or after the IV infusion (such as chills, flushing, or shortness of breath).
warnings: Infusion-related reactions can happen, especially during the first few doses, so you will be closely monitored during your infusion. Serious lung problems (called interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis) have been reported — tell your doctor right away if you have new or worsening shortness of breath or cough. Skin reactions can be severe; follow your care team's instructions for skin care. This medicine can harm an unborn baby, so use effective birth control during treatment and for a period afterward. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given through an IV (intravenous infusion) at a clinic or infusion center — you will not give it to yourself at home. The dose is based on your body weight. It is usually given once a week for the first few weeks, and then every two weeks after that. Each infusion can take several hours, so plan accordingly. Your care team will guide you on the exact schedule.
